## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6) is a treatise within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* of the Khuddaka Nikāya devoted to the analysis of the four analytical knowledges or discriminations (*paṭisambhidā*, Sanskrit *pratisamvid*): discrimination of meaning (*attha*), phenomena (*dhamma*), language (*nirutti*), and perspicuity (*paṭibhāna*) [Potter 1996]. While the classification is rare in early discourse collections, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* presumes the fundamental definitions established in chapter 15 of the *Vibhaṅga* (*Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga*) and systematically details the operation and structure of spiritual comprehension [Potter 1996]. Like much of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the chapter anchors its systematic analytical expositions in standard textual passages drawn from the Vinaya and Sutta Piṭakas [Norman 1983].
